channel.title: Volkswagen recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Volkswagen Tiguan Software Glitch Can Stall Engine
item.description: A software error can cause the body control module in the vehicle to reset itself. This can make the ignition switch off, which then stalls the engine. The same software error can also cause a loss of certain vehicle controls, warning lights, and exterior lighting. It can also cause the rearview camera system to stop working properly, affecting several parts of the vehicle at once.

item.title: VW Atlas rearview camera image may not display
item.description: These vehicles may experience a low-voltage electrical event that affects the display screen's functions. When this happens, the rearview camera image may fail to show up as it should. This affects certain Volkswagen Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles equipped with this display and camera system. Volkswagen is recalling the affected vehicles to update the rearview camera software so the image displays correctly.

item.title: Volkswagen Tiguan Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Some Volkswagen Tiguan vehicles that were previously repaired under an earlier recall have a new problem. An error can occur in the camera control unit when the vehicle starts up, which can cause the rearview camera image not to display as it should. This means the picture drivers rely on when backing up may not show up on the screen.

item.title: VW Taos Fuel Sensor May Detach in Crash
item.description: On these Taos vehicles, a fuel pressure sensor is attached to the fuel tank. If the vehicle is in a rear-end crash, that sensor may come loose or separate from the tank.

item.title: Volkswagen Jetta and Taos Instrument Panel Display Failure
item.description: The instrument panel in these vehicles may fail to show warning lights or gauges. This means the driver may not be able to see important safety information, such as the speedometer or warning lights, while driving. Not being able to see this information increases the risk of a crash. Dealers will update the instrument panel software and replace the instrument panel if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Volkswagen Jetta Ground Wire May Cause Fire Risk
item.description: On certain 2025-2026 Volkswagen Jetta vehicles, the ground wire for the transmission may not have been properly connected when the vehicle was built, leaving an open electrical circuit.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 high-voltage battery may overheat
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain ID.4 electric vehicles. The large high-voltage battery that powers the vehicle may overheat. Volkswagen says an overheating battery raises the chance of a fire. Dealers will update the battery's software and, where it is needed, replace the high-voltage battery itself. Owners were sent notification letters, and the work is carried out by Volkswagen dealers at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 high-voltage battery may catch fire
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain ID.4 electric vehicles. Inside the high-voltage battery that powers the vehicle, parts of the battery cells may be lined up incorrectly, and that can lead to a battery fire. Dealers will replace the affected battery cell modules as needed at no cost. Volkswagen mailed letters to owners in March 2026, and the vehicle identification numbers covered by this recall became searchable on the NHTSA website in January 2026.

item.title: VW Tiguan Passenger Air Bag May Deactivate
item.description: On certain Tiguan SUVs, a wiring fault in the system that detects a front passenger may cause it to turn off the front passenger air bag even when someone is sitting there.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Battery Modules Can Catch Fire
item.description: Certain Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles have high voltage battery cell modules that may contain misaligned electrodes inside them. This kind of misalignment inside the battery modules can result in a battery fire.

item.title: Volkswagen Tiguan Rear Tie Rod Bolt Loose
item.description: Certain 2025 Volkswagen Tiguan vehicles have a bolt connecting the tie rod on the rear axle assembly, and this bolt may be loose. A loose tie rod bolt on the rear axle can lead to a loss of vehicle control. This recall covers the tie rod assembly connection on the rear axle of affected Tiguan vehicles built for the 2025 model year.

item.title: VW Atlas, Atlas Cross Sport, ID.4 Loose Bolts
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain Atlas, Atlas Cross Sport and ID.4 vehicles. Some bolts in the chassis, brake system and suspension, including bolts used on parts such as the cross member, engine mount, control arm, subframe, and rear brake carrier, may not have been tightened correctly during the manufacturing process.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas Rearview Camera Image Distortion
item.description: A software error in your Volkswagen Atlas or Atlas Cross Sport can cause the rearview camera image to become distorted when you shift into reverse.

item.title: Audi Q4 E-Tron, VW ID.4 Can Lose Drive Power
item.description: In certain Audi Q4 e-tron, Q4 e-tron Sportback, and Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles, the onboard charger that keeps the 12-volt battery charged can fail and stop charging that battery. When the 12-volt battery isn't being charged, the vehicle can lose the power that drives it, meaning the car could suddenly stop moving forward while you are out on the road.

item.title: VW ID.4 Gear Position May Not Display
item.description: On certain ID.4, Audi Q4 e-Tron, and Q4 e-Tron Sportback vehicles, the instrument panel may not properly show which gear the transmission is in.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas Engine Cover May Cause Fire
item.description: Certain Volkswagen Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles may have an engine cover that was not put back on correctly after a service visit. This can let the cover come loose and touch hot parts of the engine. Dealers will remove the engine cover to fix the problem.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas Transmission Loss Of Power
item.description: Some Volkswagen Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles may have a transmission that was manufactured incorrectly. This manufacturing defect can cause the vehicle to suddenly lose drive power while it is being driven, meaning the wheels stop receiving power from the engine unexpectedly.

item.title: Volkswagen Tiguan and Audi Q3 rearview camera may not display
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain Tiguan and Arteon vehicles and certain Audi Q3 vehicles. The control unit that runs the backup camera can hit an error when the vehicle is started, and when that happens the rearview camera image does not show up the way it should. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal government's rear visibility safety standard. Dealers will install updated software for the camera control unit free of charge.

item.title: VW ID.4 Rearview Camera Image May Not Appear
item.description: On some Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles, the rearview camera image may not display when the vehicle is put into reverse or when the park function is turned on manually. The picture meant to show what's behind the vehicle can stay blank instead.

item.title: Volkswagen Beetle Driver Airbag Inflator May Explode
item.description: In certain Volkswagen Beetle and Beetle Convertible vehicles, the airbag in front of the driver can explode instead of inflating normally. This happens because the propellant inside the inflator breaks down over time, after long-term exposure to high humidity, high temperatures, and repeated temperature swings. If the inflator explodes, it can throw sharp pieces of metal at the driver or other people in the car.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas Brake Master Cylinder May Fail
item.description: The brake master cylinder in these vehicles may have been built with an incorrect part called a secondary piston spring retainer. This incorrect part can block the port that brake fluid flows through inside the master cylinder. When that fluid port becomes blocked, the brakes may not work the way they are supposed to, which means you could lose braking power while trying to stop the vehicle.

item.title: VW ID.4 Doors May Open Unexpectedly
item.description: On these Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles, water may get into the circuit board inside the door handles. This can cause a door to open unexpectedly.

item.title: VW ID.4 Passenger Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain ID4 vehicles because the fasteners holding the passenger frontal air bag inflator in place may be loose. If the inflator is not properly secured, the air bag may not deploy as intended in a crash. When an air bag does not deploy properly, it increases the risk of injury to the front seat passenger during a collision.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas and Golf backup camera may fail
item.description: On these Volkswagen vehicles, the rearview camera image may be delayed or may not turn on at all after the driver shifts the vehicle into reverse gear. Because the camera may not show the view behind the vehicle right away, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for rear visibility. Dealers will update the infotainment system software at no charge to the owner. Owner notification letters were mailed in mid-July 2024.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas passenger airbag may switch off when seat occupied
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles. The system that senses whether someone is sitting in the front passenger seat can develop a fault in its wiring. When that happens, the front passenger airbag is switched off even though a person is sitting in the seat. Dealers will replace the sensor mat in the seat together with its wiring harness to correct the problem.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Software Bug Affects Displays
item.description: A software issue in some Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles can cause the center screen and instrument panel display to fail to turn on, or to reset unexpectedly. This can cause the speedometer or rearview camera image to disappear, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Audi, VW Fuel Tank Seal May Cause Leaks
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain front-wheel-drive Audi A3, Volkswagen Golf, Golf Sportwagen, GTI, and Jetta vehicles. A seal on a suction jet pump inside the fuel tank may fail, allowing fuel to flow into the evaporative emissions system and possibly leak out of the charcoal canister. A fuel leak near a source of ignition can increase the risk of a fire. Dealers will replace the suction pump. This recall replaces an earlier recall, so vehicles already repaired under it will need the new repair.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Sunroof Shade Fails Fire Safety Standard
item.description: Certain Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles have an interior sunshade over the panoramic glass roof that is made of fabric that isn't as fire-resistant as federal safety rules require. Because of this, the vehicle doesn't meet the flammability standard for interior materials. If a fire were to start inside the vehicle, this fabric could help the fire spread further instead of resisting it the way it's supposed to.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas Side Airbag May Detach in Crash
item.description: On certain Volkswagen Atlas vehicles, the driver's side impact airbag may be missing a weld at the housing that holds it in place. Because that weld may be missing, the airbag could fail to deploy the way it's supposed to, or it could come loose, if the vehicle is ever in a crash. This increases the risk of injury to people riding in the vehicle if a crash happens.

item.title: Volkswagen Jetta may not chime for key left in ignition
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain 2019 Jetta vehicles. The instrument cluster may not sound the audible warning that tells the driver the key is still in the ignition when the door is open. Because that warning may not sound, these vehicles do not meet the federal theft protection rule. Dealers will update the instrument cluster free of charge. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed November 3, 2023. Volkswagen's number for this recall is 90W7.

item.title: VW Golf, GTI, Jetta Ignition Switch Can Fail
item.description: On certain Volkswagen Golf, Golf Alltrack, Golf Sportwagen, Golf GTI, and Jetta vehicles with a conventional ignition switch, the switch itself may fail, and this is more likely in high-temperature conditions. If the switch fails, the vehicle's electrical system can shut down and the engine can stall while you are driving, cutting power in the middle of a drive.

item.title: VW Atlas Engine Connecting Rod Bearing Failure Risk
item.description: In some Volkswagen Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport SUVs, the bearings on the engine's connecting rods may become damaged, which can cause the engine to fail. When the engine fails, the vehicle can stall while it is being driven, and the failure may also cause an oil leak. Oil leaking from the engine can increase the chance of a fire.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Software Bug Delays Rearview Camera
item.description: Some vehicles received a replacement infotainment control unit during an earlier repair that has the wrong software installed. That software problem can cause the rearview camera image to be delayed or to not show up at all when you shift into reverse.

item.title: Volkswagen Golf R Suspension Strut Mount May Loosen
item.description: The mount that holds the front suspension strut in place may be deformed, or bent out of shape. When that happens, the bolted connections holding the strut to the suspension can come loose.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Doors May Open While Driving
item.description: Some door handles may have let water reach the circuit board inside them. If this happens, the affected door can open on its own while the vehicle is moving and experiencing strong sideways force at low speeds. A door opening unexpectedly while driving increases the chance that someone in the vehicle could be injured.

item.title: Volkswagen Taos Fuel Pump May Cause Stalling
item.description: In certain 2022 Volkswagen Taos vehicles, the fuel delivery pump may break. If it breaks, the engine can suddenly stall while the vehicle is being driven. A sudden stall like this can increase the chance of a crash.

item.title: VW Atlas Passenger Air Bag Can Deactivate
item.description: On certain Volkswagen Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles, a wiring fault in the system that senses whether the front passenger seat is occupied can cause the front passenger air bag to switch off even when someone is sitting in that seat. If a crash happens while the air bag is switched off, it will not be there to help protect the passenger.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Battery Software May Cut Drive Power
item.description: In some Volkswagen ID.4 vehicles, a software issue can cause the high-voltage battery management control module to restart on its own, or cause the pulse inverter to shut off.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Battery Cable Wear May Cause Short
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain ID4 rear-wheel drive vehicles because the 12-volt battery charging cable may contact the steering column shaft, causing the cable's insulation to wear and possibly resulting in a short circuit.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 Coolant Leak Into High-Voltage System
item.description: Volkswagen is recalling certain ID4 vehicles because a sealing ring on the electric motor was not assembled correctly. This can allow coolant to leak into the vehicle's high-voltage electrical system, which may interfere with onboard communication and the power supply. That interference can affect safety-critical systems and warning lights in the vehicle.
